description: FüSim Digital is a web-based simulation system for training emergency services leadership personnel to manage mass casualty incidents (MCI) and other major incidents. It began as a digital version of FüSim MANV, a German table-top simulation for emergency medical services leaders. A trainer builds an exercise by placing patients, vehicles with material and personnel, viewports, transfer points and hospitals on a map; participants join, each possibly restricted to one area, and once the exercise starts untreated patients deteriorate and may die, so participants must triage, treat, coordinate by radio and transport patients to hospitals. It is developed in the hpi-sam GitHub organisation, whose name points to the Hasso Plattner Institute in Germany. Coverage: any incident site on the map; the model is designed around German EMS organisation, and resolution is the individual patient, vehicle and person. It runs in the browser at fuesim.digital, and the TypeScript source is on GitHub for self-hosting. Licence: GNU AGPL v3, free. Caveats: it is a training simulator whose patient deterioration follows exercise scripts, not validated clinical models, and releases are still candidates (1.0.0 release candidates). Simulation uses: emergency response training and exercising of hospital and ambulance capacity during mass casualty incidents. Related records: none catalogued yet; ambulance operations models include JEMSS (catalogued as model-jemss).
